Why does expect(['a']).toBe(['a']) fail? What do you use?
a: toBe checks it is the SAME array in memory; two arrays created separately are different. Use toEqual to compare the content.

q: Two sort() gotchas?
a: 1) Without a compare function, numbers are sorted as text ([1, 10, 100, 9]); use (a, b) => a - b. 2) sort() changes the original; sort a copy: [...list].sort().

q: map vs filter vs find: what does each give back?
a: map: a new array of the same length (each item transformed). filter: a new array with the items whose callback returned true. find: the FIRST matching item itself (or undefined).

q: Can you push into an array declared with const?
a: Yes. const means you can't assign a different array to the variable (cart = []), but the content can change (push, pop, sort).

q: After `const first = names.find(...)`, `first.length` gives "'first' is possibly 'undefined'." Why?
a: find returns undefined when nothing matches, so its type is string | undefined. Check it first, use first?.length, or assert it with expect.
